No — stop and escalate instead of implementing it.

Here's why: the ticket has an explicit non-goal ("don't touch shared auth middleware"), and you've now hit 3 failed attempts at the stated goal (timeout, retry, clock mock) without crossing that line. That's the trigger to stop retrying variants and check in with whoever owns the ticket, not to unilaterally expand scope — especially since the middleware is shared with other services, so a rewrite has blast radius beyond this test/CI concern.

What I'd do:
1. Write up the three attempts and why each still leaves ~1-in-5 flakiness (this is useful evidence).
2. Flag to the ticket owner that the root cause appears to live in the session-expiry logic itself, and a real fix likely requires touching shared auth middleware — which the ticket explicitly excludes.
3. Let them decide: expand scope with buy-in from whoever owns the shared middleware (and its other consumers), split it into a separate ticket, or accept a narrower mitigation (e.g., quarantine/mark the test as flaky with a tracking issue) for now.

If they green-light the middleware change, that becomes a new, explicitly scoped piece of work with its own review from stakeholders of the other services — not a quiet addition to this ticket. Want help drafting that escalation note or documenting the three failed attempts?
